clue.text: Call me before this lady's show

definitions.text: Call me before this lady's show

parts.words: Call me before this lady's show
parts.note: a show whose title begins 'Call Me' and ends with a polite word for a lady: the Irving Berlin musical about an American woman ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone is told to address a woman a certain way before her performance.
explanation.walkthrough: Call Me Madam is a 1950 Broadway musical; the polite title for a lady completes its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical's title ends with the respectful form of address used for a woman.

clue.text: Stayed in us state, getting into debt

indicators.note: one piece getting into another means it is placed inside it

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt, so debt gives red
Maine is a US state in New England

explanation.surface: A traveller lingered in an American state while running up debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts MAINE inside RED, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To have stayed is to have lingered on in one place, a past tense synonym.

clue.text: Within the team?

parts.note: a side is a team in sport, so being in it is being in the side

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone belongs to the squad.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on the interior of something; a side is a sports team, so 'in side' is also within the team.

clue.text: End-point

explanation.surface: A terse definition of a final destination.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something to a halt is to end it, and a full stop is the punctuation point closing a sentence.

clue.text: Try to bring in American tank first, it's reliable

indicators.note: the word try is asked to bring in other letters, so they go inside it
the first letter of the word tank is taken

explanation.surface: An instruction to deploy an American tank ahead of others because it is dependable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes T from 'tank'; 'to bring in' puts US and T inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A trusty companion or tool is one you can depend upon, a synonym.

clue.text: Idiotically fighting, I slay nine

indicators.note: fighting letters are in turmoil, signalling that these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boastful warrior claims to have killed nine opponents, foolishly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' rearranges the letters of I SLAY NINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Asinine means donkey-like, stupid, so the adverb means in a foolish way.

clue.text: Motherhood has a bad name — try it

indicators.note: a bad version of the words is a corrupted one, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being a mother is said to carry a poor reputation, but give it a go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges the letters of NAME and TRY IT together; 'has a' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: The state of being a mother; maternity is the noun for that condition.

clue.text: Disgusting to take such a large quantity!

explanation.surface: Someone recoils at being expected to eat a huge portion.
explanation.definitionFit: Gross means repulsive, and as a number it is twelve dozen, one hundred and forty-four items.

clue.text: Note from the landlord

explanation.surface: A message arrives from the person you rent from.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter is a written message, and someone who lets out property is literally one who lets.

clue.text: Said goodbye to me on the mat

parts.note: ta-ta is a casual spoken farewell
mi (or me) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone bade farewell while standing on the doormat.
explanation.walkthrough: MI is the sol-fa note sometimes spelt 'me', as in do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatami is a traditional Japanese floor covering of woven straw.

clue.text: Nice, once the rustic has left

indicators.note: the rustic has a letter within him, so the letter is placed inside

parts.note: a peasant is a country labourer, a rustic

explanation.surface: Life became agreeable once the country bumpkin had gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' could be the French city, but here it is the adjective; 'has' puts L inside PEASANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice and pleasant are synonyms for agreeable.

clue.text: Mean to put in $10

parts.note: ten dollars: TEN for the number and D, an abbreviation for dollar

explanation.surface: Someone plans to contribute a ten-dollar note.
explanation.walkthrough: The dollar sign stands for D (dollar), placed after the ten; 'to put' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean to do something is to plan or purpose it, a synonym.

clue.text: He'll sink to any depths for money

definitions.text: He'll sink to any depths for money

parts.words: He'll sink to any depths for money
parts.note: reads like an unscrupulous person, but literally describes someone who goes underwater professionally, such as a pearl hunter

explanation.surface: A description of a person who will do anything shameful for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional underwater worker literally descends deep in the sea for pay.

clue.text: Taste gin cocktail after straining

indicators.note: the mixed letters come after the first piece

parts.note: to try food is to taste it

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the word gin is mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone samples a gin drink after passing it through a sieve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cocktail' rearranges GIN to ING, which comes 'after' TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Trying means taxing or stressful, as straining does.

clue.text: Embarrassed at having lost vitality

explanation.surface: A person is humiliated at being worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Mortified means deeply ashamed, and mortified flesh is dead tissue, no longer living.

clue.text: A link to James?

explanation.surface: A question whether something connects to a man named James.
explanation.definitionFit: A bond is a tie or connection, and James Bond is Ian Fleming's spy.

clue.text: Perform live with rector on the organ

parts.note: to perform live is to be on stage live, giving the word live
R is the abbreviation for rector, a parish clergyman

explanation.surface: A musician plays a concert with the parish priest at the church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' suggests the church instrument, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: The liver is a large glandular body part, an organ.

clue.text: Real wild party for wild west town?

indicators.note: wild suggests out of control, so the letters of the word real are scrambled

explanation.surface: A raucous celebration in a frontier settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' rearranges REAL to LARE; DO is added. The second 'wild' is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Laredo is a Texas border town of cowboy-era fame, a classic setting of Western stories.

clue.text: Run from lightning

explanation.surface: Someone flees a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolt is to dash away, and a bolt is a flash of electricity in a storm.

clue.text: Breakdowns in relations affecting each Serb

indicators.note: affecting means altering, so the words each Serb have their letters altered

explanation.surface: Diplomatic ruptures having an impact on every Serbian citizen.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaches are ruptures or rifts between parties, as in a breach of friendship.

clue.text: He'll keep you fired up!

parts.note: sounds like a motivator, but literally describes a man who feeds a furnace to keep it burning

explanation.surface: A rousing promise from someone who keeps morale high.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who tends a boiler or engine furnace, shovelling coal to keep it alight.

clue.text: Massages, we're told, are necessities

indicators.note: we're told means we hear it spoken, signalling a word that sounds the same

explanation.surface: A claim that back rubs are essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we're told' signals a homophone: needs and the answer are pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneading is working muscles with the hands, as in a massage.

clue.text: A pop artist — and his critic

explanation.surface: A hip-hop musician and the reviewer who slates him.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapper is a hip-hop performer, and one who raps, or censures sharply, is a critic.

clue.text: Colours of underclothes I wear?

indicators.note: I wear the underclothes, so they go around I

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the hue of the underwear they have on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wear' puts the underclothes around I; in Britain pants are underwear, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Paints are colouring substances, colours in an artist's box.

clue.text: Amorous soccer coach has extra energy between six and eight

indicators.note: the coach has something extra within him, so a letter is added inside

parts.note: Sven-Goran Eriksson, the England football manager, much reported for his love affairs

explanation.surface: A womanising football manager has surplus vigour between six and eight o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Sven-Goran Eriksson managed England's football team (2001-06) and his affairs filled the British tabloids.
explanation.definitionFit: The number following six and preceding eight in counting.

clue.text: Is he criminally tactless?

parts.note: a lawbreaker is also, literally, one who causes offence, as a tactless person does

explanation.surface: A question whether a person's rudeness amounts to a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawbreaker or culprit; literally one who offends, as a tactless person upsets people.

clue.text: Reduce sail — rocks in sight!

explanation.surface: A sailor's urgent order on spotting danger ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To reef is to shorten sail by rolling it, and a reef is a ridge of rock near the sea's surface.

clue.text: Measurements taken of small islands

explanation.surface: Survey readings taken of some little islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Inch (from Gaelic innis) is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: An inch is a unit of length, and in Scotland an inch is a small island.

clue.text: Bows one can attach to hairpin

explanation.surface: Ribbon decorations one fastens to a hair clip.
explanation.definitionFit: Bends are curves or bows, and a hairpin bend is a sharp U-shaped turn in a road.

clue.text: Made drink, having set out then scattered

indicators.note: brewed is having letters inside it, so they are placed within

parts.note: to brew is to make tea or beer, so made drink gives brewed

indicators.note: set out suggests disorder, so the word set is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone made a drink having laid things out, then spilled it everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET to EST; 'having' puts it inside BREWED after the B; 'then' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestrewed is an old word meaning strewn about, covered with things spread around.
